messages:
Mia: Heads up — trying to bring up atelier-11b (hf:atelier/atelier-11b-v2) for benchmarking/quant experiments. License looks... restrictive.
Liam: link?
Mia: https://huggingface.co/atelier/atelier-11b-v2/blob/main/LICENSE.txt
Mia: key clauses: `research-only`, `no commercial deployment`, `attribution required`, and a weird `no-hosting` paragraph. pasted snippet:
```
Section 2. Use Restrictions: The weights and model may be used for research and evaluation only. Commercial use, hosting, serving, or deployment for revenue generation is prohibited without explicit written license from the Authors. Redistribution of model weights or derivatives is not permitted.
```
Liam: ouch. so no Hosted API or dedicated offering without a separate license, right? :grimacing:
Sophia: cc @Legal. From a quick read: "research-only" + "no hosting" = we cannot expose this via Redwood Hosted. We need an explicit commercial license for any external/paid use.
Legal-Bot: Summary: research/restricted. Hosting/serving/redistribution disallowed. Possible paths: 1) ask authors for commercial license; 2) run internally on Private with author permission + indemnity; 3) decline. This is not a clear "open" permissive license.
Nora: technical note: I ran int8 quant (GPTQ) in staging and saw ~4.1% drop on our summarization eval suite vs fp16 baseline. Latency improves ~2.3x. So it's a tradeoff we were excited about.
Jamal: If authors grant a license that allows hosting, ops needs a signed grant that explicitly permits serving + redistribution of quantized weights. Otherwise we can only run on customer-managed Private deployments (on-prem/VPC) if terms allow.
Mia: On the redistribution point: they explicitly forbid "redistribution of model weights or derivatives." That would rule out us shipping quantized binaries or including weights in a dedicated image customers download.
Sophia: Exactly. For Dedicated we could potentially host in our infra if the license permits "serving" but forbids redistribution. For Private deployments where customers get the weights, that would likely violate the clause unless the license says otherwise.
Liam: Is there precedent? did we ever request a commercial addendum for other models?
Sophia: Yes — we negotiated a commercial addendum with the authors of "raven-13b" last year. Typical ask: limited hosting rights, attribution clause, revenue share or one-time fee, and indemnity.
Nora: Practically speaking, if authors won't allow redistribution, we could still support quant experiments as long as we don't persist or share the quantized weights outside the staging instance. But that's awkward for evals and production rollouts.
Mia: Action items: I'll email the authors asking (1) commercial hosting/license for Redwood Hosted + Dedicated, (2) whether redistribution of quantized/derivative weights is permitted under a paid license, (3) attribution/legal text they require.
Sophia: I'll prep a legal checklist for the ask (clauses we need: hosting rights, redistribution, attribution language, indemnity, export controls).
Jamal: I'll prototype a gated staging flow where we run quantized experiments in a non-persistent environment (no weights exported) so evals can continue while we await license.
Nora: FYI bench details: int8 (GPTQ) config I used: `--group-size 128 --quantize-weights --no-triton` and eval script `bench/summarize_eval.py`. Perf numbers saved to /tmp/atelier_int8_run1.log.
Mia: Thanks. @Sophia do you want me to include bench numbers in the email to make the commercial ask stronger?
Sophia: yes include perf + regression delta and target SLOs; helps negotiation. Also ask for an enterprise license template if they have one.
Liam: ping me if authors push back — we might propose a limited pilot license for a few customers.
Legal-Bot: Logging action: opened ticket INF-4342 to track license outreach and attach bench logs.
Mia: Cool. I'll post updates in this thread. For now: stop any downstream packaging of weights until we hear back. :white_check_mark:
